newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico troops hunt Marxist rebels after attack.
newsitem.headline: Mexico troops hunt Marxist rebels after attack.

text.p: Hundreds of troops combed the rugged mountains of Mexico's impoverished state of Guerrero on Wednesday, searching for Marxist rebels who waged a gunbattle in which at least five people died.

Helicopter gunships and small aircraft flew overhead as combat troops fanned out across the Pacific coast region, which lies between the tourist resorts of Acapulco and Ixtapa, about 150 miles (250 km) southwest of Mexico City.
Armoured personnel carriers rumbled along the dusty roads, machine guns at the ready. Jeeps, one bearing bulletholes and one stained with blood at the rear, followed behind.
Rifle-toting troops prevented reporters from reaching the scene of Tuesday's attacks by the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), the group's second armed strike in four days.

The local military command said three soldiers and two unidentified gunmen were killed in Tuesday's incidents, which took place in the hot, dusty peasant town of Atoyac de Alvarez, some 40 miles (62 km) northwest of Acapulco.

In Mexico City, federal government officials did their best to play down the attacks. The Defence Ministry, the Interior Ministry and the presidency all either failed to take calls or said they had no information about the incident beyond the 11-line army statement issued Tuesday.

Most Mexican media, which are heavily influenced by the government, also played down the attacks. Many followed the army statement in labelling the attackers as "armed individuals" rather than EPR rebels.
But in the town of Atoyac, reporters saw the bodies of two men brought to a morgue bearing olive green uniforms with bandannas round their necks and military boots.

"Their uniforms don't have anything that explicitly states EPR on them. But we presume from their uniforms, their boots, their weapons and the covering of their faces, everything indicates they are members of the EPR", said Efrain Mendoza Ortiz, a local prosecutor investigating the incident.

A military official in Guerrero, who wished to remain anonymous, also told Reuters Tuesday evening that the gunmen had been identified as members of the Marxist EPR, which first appeared in the state at the end of June 1996 calling for the overthrow of President Ernesto Zedillo's government.
The official also said at least 10 other soldiers were wounded in Tuesday's attacks but this could not be confirmed.
